intended_object: The linear projection of a module E onto a submodule p along a complementary submodule q (E = p ⊕ q). It is the unique linear map E → p that is the identity on p and zero on q. This comes from the docstring.
explanation:
The body inverts the linear isomorphism p × q ≃ E, (x, y) ↦ x + y. This isomorphism exists because p and q are complements. Composing the inverse with the first projection sends x = x_p + x_q to x_p. That is exactly the projection onto p along q, so it is the identity on p and zero on q, as the docstring says.

Working over a ring (rather than a semiring) is the natural setting. Over a semiring, IsCompl in the lattice of submodules does not in general give the internal direct-sum decomposition, because that argument uses subtraction. So the definition is not too narrow.

This is in fact Mathlib's own declaration, the renamed version of the old `Submodule.linearProjOfIsCompl`; the deprecated alias at line 794 points to it. The `LinearMap.linearProjOfIsCompl` at line 346, which I give as the counterpart, is a separate variant that projects along a complement of the range of an injective linear map.
